caption: Each dot is one or more recorded tests from the experimental tables of the 24 NASA PSI investigations used here: the 878 tests with a recorded ambient oxygen value, from 7 of the investigations, all run in microgravity. Also drawn: atmospheres cited from NASA documents and the challenge statement, and the team's own presets and counting ranges. A plot by the team; a dot means a test was run at that oxygen level, not that anything burned or went out; a dot near a target atmosphere does not mean the test represents that atmosphere, because fuel, flow, pressure, balance gas and gravity can differ; not operational safety guidance.
Oxygen percent alone does not define an atmosphere; pressure and balance gas are shown where the table records them.
Gas-burner flames that emulate condensed fuels (PSI-20) were run at listed oxygen concentrations up to 40% (approximate, as the table notes say); that table is per test day and is not plotted.

Outside PSI, Table 1 of the paper 'Preliminary Results from the Saffire VI Experiment' (ICES-2024-365) lists the sample test conditions of the five Saffire IV to VI samples considered in that paper, from 22.0 to 31.0 mol % oxygen and 54.1 to 100.0 kPa (cited, never counted); none of the 24 PSI investigations used here is one of these flights; the values were read from the paper by an AI assistant and not checked by a person.

flex.status_note: for 1 of the 1 test without a pressure value, the NASA cell holds a value that the pipeline flags and does not use (see empty_reasons and the point's value_flags); that cell is not empty

oxidizer_stream.why: Oxygen of the oxidizer stream of an inverse flame (o2_basis 'oxidizer_stream') is not the oxygen of an atmosphere a crew breathes, so these tests are never mixed with the ambient points.

no_ambient_oxygen_value.rule: Tests with no o2_basis, or with o2_basis 'ambient' and an empty o2_pct: the table records no oxygen value for them. Not recorded is not zero.

targets.label: Team counting range for 'ISS cabin' (the team's choice, used for the need counts; drawn dashed)
targets.as_written: Oxygen and pressure ranges are the coverage bins around 21% and 101.3 kPa (coverage.json): 19 to 23% oxygen and 85.8 to below 116.8 kPa. The oxygen range is the +/-2.0 point control box that EAWG.atmospheres recommends around its own nominal atmospheres, used here as a bin; the pressure range is the team's bin and is wider than the +/-0.2 psia box of the same item. No reference item gives an ISS operating range for oxygen or pressure. Flow is the normal ISS ventilation range (ICES19.issflow). The ranges set no balance gas: the count of matched tests with carbon dioxide or helium added to the atmosphere is given next to the tier.
targets.access_note: the team's own range (data role, pipeline/spec/scenarios.json)

targets.label: Team counting range for 'Lunar base or pressurized rover' (the team's choice, used for the need counts; drawn dashed); its pressure range (below 85.8 kPa) is wider than the 70.3 kPa (10.2 psi) of the challenge statement
targets.as_written: The challenge text gives oxygen likely 30% or more and 10.2 psi (70.3 kPa) or less. Oxygen is capped at 36% (highest design value 34% plus 2 points); the cap is the team's and is not in the challenge text, so a test above 36% oxygen is marked outside the range. Pressure uses the coverage bins around and below 70.3 kPa, because tests set to 0.7 atm are recorded at 70.2 to 72.6 kPa; the range therefore reaches up to 85.8 kPa, above the 70.3 kPa of the bound, and the FLEX tests matched on oxygen and pressure are recorded at 71.2 to 72.4 kPa in the current tables. No flow range is given for this environment. The pair is a bound taken from the challenge statement (CH.moonbase: oxygen likely 30% or more, pressure 10.2 psi or less; checked on the official page by another session of the team on 2026-11-14); NASA Task Book 14639 names 30% oxygen at 10.2 psia as the most severe test environment (TB14639.worstcase). Nominal values are the bound, not a design point.
targets.access_note: the team's own range (data role, pipeline/spec/scenarios.json)

Oxygen is 34 +/- 2 points (the EAWG control box applied to 34%); pressure is the coverage bin below 62.8 kPa, so any recorded pressure below 62.8 kPa is inside the range. The 62.8 kPa edge is the midpoint between 8.0 psia (55.2 kPa) and 10.2 psia (70.3 kPa), not between 8.2 psia and 10.2 psia. No gravity level is set. Not a scorer preset.

tests_gas_fractions_not_summing_to_1.rule: For tables with a nitrogen column, the oxygen, nitrogen and added-gas fractions of the NASA row are summed as written; a point lists the sums that differ from 1 by more than 0.005. Reported, not corrected.

rules.plotted: A test is plotted when tests.csv gives o2_basis 'ambient' and an o2_pct value. Points group tests with the same fuel_phase, investigation_id, o2_pct, pressure_kpa (or no pressure value) and balance_gas; values are used as written in tests.csv, not binned.
rules.balance_gas: n2_only: the table has a nitrogen column and every added-gas column it has (carbon dioxide, helium) is 0 for the test; co2_added / he_added: that column is above 0; not_recorded: the table has no added-gas column, or the cell is empty. Views draw co2_added and he_added as hollow markers.
rules.pressure_kpa_null: Null means the map has no pressure value for the test: pressure is not a column of the table, or the cell is empty, or the cell holds a value the pipeline does not use (see pressure_column and the point's value_flags). Null is never drawn as 0 and never as 101 kPa.
